title: On-the-fly divergence detector for warmed-KV responses with minimal-rewrite replay harness
creator: Marin K. Zhou
description: Problem: We observe rare but user-visible output divergences when a request hits a warmed KV/prefix cache vs when the same request is served cold. Existing regression suites focus on batch audits and golden-response comparisons but lack a lightweight, on-path detector that flags divergence at the time of rollout or config change. Goal: build an on-the-fly divergence detector that compares warmed-hit responses to minimal-rewrite cold replays and surfaces signal grouped by prefix, model-variant, and config fingerprint. The harness should be cheap enough to run in canaries and during config rollouts, and produce ranked example pairs with automatic heuristics for semantic vs trivial token differences.
acceptance_criteria: 1) A detector service (serverless probe) that, given a live request and a warmed-KV hit, can replay a minimal cold path request and produce a diff pair within 2x the normal request latency budget for canary mode (target: median < 300ms extra).

2) The system must label diffs as 'token-noise' vs 'semantic-change' using hybrid heuristics (edit-distance threshold + embedding cosine + rule-based canonicalization), with a configurable threshold exposed in the console.
3) Auto-ingest top-100 divergence examples into an S3 bucket and expose a per-rollout dashboard showing divergence rate by prefix, model variant, and config fingerprint.
4) Integration with rollout gating: canary fails if semantic-change rate > 0.5% on a 5k-sample window for high-risk prefixes (list configurable).

5) Unit + integration tests that simulate KV-hit warm responses and corresponding replayed cold responses across at least 3 model families (decoder-only, encoder-decoder, chat-style) with deterministic fixtures.
6) Documentation (Confluence + Console help) describing probe cost, privacy considerations, and steps to opt out for sensitive prefixes.
proposed_approach: Phase A: lightweight probe (canary) — run probe in shadow mode for 2 weeks. For each warmed-hit, issue a low-priority cold replay routed to a minimal cold-serving path (may be lower-tier model if identical weights unavailable). Persist pair for offline scoring.
Phase B: on-path detector — implement synchronous check for manual rollouts where latency overhead budget exists; use async fallback for regular traffic.
Phase C: gating + alerting — wire detector outputs into trials: console alert, rollout block, and nightly regression report.

Trade-offs considered: cost vs coverage (sampling heuristics), privacy (redaction/PII handling during replay), and fidelity when exact model variants or quantization differ between warm and replay paths.

Fallback plan: if a faithful cold re-execution is impossible, capture the minimal upstream trace + tokens and run a shadow approximate replay with alignment heuristics; surface lower confidence label.
progress_updates: 2025-02-18: Kickoff meeting with runtime, infra, and console teams. Agreed to prototype using a shadow-lambda style probe for canary traffic. (Notes: Confluence link below).
2025-02-22: Prototype spike completed — proof-of-concept cold replay via dedicated canary pool. Replayed 1200 warmed-hit samples, observed 0.7% semantic-change baseline on curated prefix set.
2025-02-26: Design review with PM and Design — decided to expose threshold controls in Console rollout modal and to add 'sensitive prefix' opt-out. Action: PM to draft console copy (PM link).

2025-03-03: First internal PR opened for the probe agent and replay harness (https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/2147). Initial CI failing due to fixture nondeterminism; working with model-onboarding team to pin seeds.
2025-03-04: Added embedding-based semantic scorer to reduce false positives from punctuation and tokenization drift. Local tests show precision improvement from 78% -> 91% on our dev set.
Next: complete dashboard tiles, add gating hook, write regression smoke tests, and schedule 2-week shadow run.
decisions: Use hybrid heuristic (edit-distance + embedding similarity) as primary signal rather than full eval suite to keep canary cost low.
Replay path may use the nearest compatible model variant when an exact binary match is unavailable; record mismatch confidence.
Probe sampling: default 1% of traffic for non-critical prefixes, 10% for high-risk prefixes during rollouts.
Persist raw paired examples in encrypted S3 with KMS key tagged to rollout ID; retention default 90 days.
Expose a 'block on semantic regressions' toggle in the Console rollout flow.
risks_mitigations: Risk: Replaying requests could leak PII. Mitigation: redact defined fields at ingress and run replay on redacted payloads; mark prefixes as sensitive to opt out.
Risk: Cost of cold replays at scale. Mitigation: aggressive sampling, use lower-capacity model variants for approximate replay, and cap per-rollout budget.
Risk: False positives due to tokenization updates. Mitigation: canonicalize whitespace/punctuation and include tokenizer version in fingerprint.
links: Regression corpus S3 (read-only links require auth): s3://redwood-evals/warmed-kv/examples/2025-02-spike/
testing_plan: Unit tests for canonicalization pipeline and embedding scorer with seeded randomness.
Integration test: run 5k synthetic prefixed requests through warm+replay path and assert divergence labeling matches golden annotations >= 90% precision.
Shadow canary: 14-day run on canary tier for top-500 prefixes with daily summaries and weekly human review sampling.
CI job: nondeterminism detector to fail PRs if replay fixtures are flaky beyond threshold.
notes_for_reviewer: Focus review on API surface between probe agent and replay controller: we want minimal coupling to avoid heavy infra changes.
Review the privacy redaction list and confirm alignment with Legal.
Validate storage encryption + lifecycle policy for paired examples.
